valores.label: Federal law names Juneau the temporary seat of government; government stays in Sitka (June 6, 1900)
Law creating the Territory of Alaska puts the capital at Juneau (Aug. 24, 1912)

fonte: U.S. Statutes at Large; Governor of Alaska (U.S. Department of the Interior)
legenda: How the capital came to Juneau, in three steps.
credito_tela: Source: U.S. Statutes at Large, 1900 and 1912; Governor of Alaska, 1906
nota: As três fontes são federais (domínio público). O Internet Archive é só o hospedeiro da digitalização do relatório federal de 1906 (texto, não mídia); o §7.3 da midia.md trata de acervo de imagem e vídeo. O crédito de dado federal é opcional (identidade.md §7 dispensa crédito de mídia em domínio público); a linha sugerida é do redator decidir.
narracao: In 1900, a federal law named Juneau the temporary seat of government, but the government stayed in Sitka… The governor's office moved to Juneau in 1906. And the 1912 law creating the Territory of Alaska was plain: "the capital of the Territory of Alaska shall be at the city of Juneau, Alaska."

conferencia.item: 1900, sede provisória em Juneau, governo em Sitka
conferencia.prova: "The temporary seat of government of said district is hereby established at Juneau: Provided, That the seat of government shall remain at Sitka until suitable grounds and buildings thereon shall be obtained…"

conferencia.item: 1906, o gabinete do governador muda para Juneau
conferencia.localizador: Report of the Governor of Alaska, p. 3
conferencia.prova: "…and on September 8 moved the executive office to Juneau."

"Sec. 2. Capital at Juneau.—That the capital of the Territory of Alaska shall be at the city of Juneau, Alaska, and the seat of government shall be maintained there." A citação da voz bate letra a letra com o trecho entre aspas.
